l4_steps.name: Crew sign-in and duty period validation
l4_steps.input: Scheduled report time, crew roster assignment
l4_steps.output: Validated duty start time, confirmed crew pairing
l4_steps.kpi: Sign-in completion ≥30 min prior to departure; FTL compliance 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 117 / EASA FTL limits require real-time cumulative duty tracking across time zones — late roster updates in Jeppesen Crew Management can create compliance gaps at sign-in

l4_steps.name: Validate fatigue risk and FTL compliance
l4_steps.input: Cumulative flight hours, rest period log, duty start time
l4_steps.output: FTL compliance confirmation or crew relief trigger
l4_steps.kpi: FTL violation rate <0.1% of monthly departures
l4_steps.pain_point: Fatigue Risk Management System (FRMS) data is not always integrated with real-time crew tracking; manual overrides by Crew Scheduling introduce compliance risk during IROPS

l4_steps.name: Retrieve and open crew briefing package
l4_steps.output: Loaded briefing package: flight plan, weather, NOTAMs, ATIS
l4_steps.kpi: Briefing package retrieval within 2 min of sign-in; package currency ≤60 min old at review
l4_steps.pain_point: EFB synchronisation delays on congested airport Wi-Fi (especially at hub gates) can result in crews accessing stale briefing data — no automatic staleness alert in FliteDeck

l4_steps.name: Review METAR, TAF, and SIGMET reports
l4_steps.input: Current METAR, TAF for departure/en-route/destination, SIGMETs
l4_steps.output: Crew weather assessment and ceiling/visibility minima check
l4_steps.kpi: Weather briefing completed ≥20 min before STD; 100% SIGMET acknowledgement logged
l4_steps.pain_point: Rapidly evolving convective SIGMETs issued by NOAA Aviation Weather Center can be uploaded to GoDirect with 10–15 min latency — crew may depart with outdated convective picture

l4_steps.name: Assess destination and alternate minima
l4_steps.input: Terminal aerodrome forecasts, instrument approach plate minima, airline OpSpecs
l4_steps.output: Alternate airport selection and additional fuel requirement
l4_steps.kpi: Correct alternate selected per ICAO Annex 2 / FAR 121.619; fuel-to-alternate margin ≥45 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Low-visibility operations (Cat II/III) require special OpSpecs approval in FAA WebOPSS; not all airports in the network have current CAT II/III plates loaded in FliteDeck for all aircraft types

l4_steps.name: Confirm weather acceptable for planned departure
l4_steps.input: Weather assessment, crew minimums, operational limits
l4_steps.output: Go / No-Go weather decision; delay or reroute request if no-go
l4_steps.kpi: Weather-related departure decision communicated to OCC ≥15 min before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Dispatcher and Captain may reach independent weather conclusions using different data sources (GoDirect vs airline wx feed) with no reconciliation workflow — leads to coordination delays at the gate

l4_steps.name: Review computerised flight plan and fuel load
l4_steps.input: Filed ATC flight plan, optimised route, fuel figures from Dispatch
l4_steps.output: Reviewed flight plan with crew acknowledgement
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan review complete ≥15 min before STD; fuel uplift variance ≤2% vs planned
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE flight plan generation relies on current NOTAM and airspace restriction feeds; late TFR activations (military, VIP) can invalidate the planned route after the plan has been generated but before crew signs off

l4_steps.name: Review dispatch release for regulatory compliance
l4_steps.input: Dispatch release document, OpSpecs authorisations, fuel release
l4_steps.output: Crew review annotation; list of queries for Dispatcher
l4_steps.kpi: Dispatch release co-sign rate without amendment ≥92%; amendment resolution time ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Dispatch releases generated in NAVBLUE are not dynamically linked to MEL deferral records in Boeing Toolbox — Captain must manually cross-check deferred items against the release, increasing error risk under time pressure

l4_steps.name: Co-sign dispatch release with Dispatcher
l4_steps.output: Dual-signed dispatch release (FAR 121.663 joint responsibility established)
l4_steps.kpi: Dispatch release signed ≥10 min before STD; 100% digital co-signature audit trail
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 121.663 requires both Captain and Dispatcher to hold the release jointly — paper-based release at remote stations without NAVBLUE access creates audit trail gaps and scan-to-file delays

l4_steps.name: Review NOTAM package for departure and en-route
l4_steps.input: NOTAM filter output for departure airport, en-route waypoints, destination
l4_steps.output: Annotated NOTAM list; crew awareness of active restrictions
l4_steps.kpi: NOTAM review complete prior to departure; safety-critical NOTAMs (runway closures, ILS unserviceable) flagged 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: NOTAM volume has increased >300% since 2010 (FAA data); FliteDeck's automated filtering still surfaces 80–120 NOTAMs per flight, creating information overload and risk that critical items are missed

l4_steps.name: Review MEL and CDL deferred item list
l4_steps.input: Aircraft tail number, active MEL/CDL deferrals, maintenance logbook
l4_steps.output: Crew acceptance or rejection of aircraft with deferred items
l4_steps.kpi: MEL review completion rate 100% prior to boarding; deferral-related delays <0.5% of departures
l4_steps.pain_point: MEL records in Boeing Toolbox are updated by Maintenance Control but real-time sync to crew EFB (FliteDeck) is not guaranteed — crews may board an aircraft unaware of a late deferral logged after their briefing

l4_steps.name: Confirm airworthiness release from Maintenance
l4_steps.input: Signed aircraft logbook, maintenance release certificate
l4_steps.output: Airworthiness confirmed; aircraft released for service
l4_steps.kpi: Maintenance release issued ≥45 min before STD; 100% release traceability in AMOS
l4_steps.pain_point: Maintenance release signature workflows in AMOS require LMB engineer to physically sign the tech log — at outstations without AMOS connectivity, paper tech logs create a digitisation lag and potential duplicate entry errors

l4_steps.name: Conduct pre-flight exterior walk-around
l4_steps.output: Completed exterior inspection record; any defects raised
l4_steps.kpi: Walk-around completed ≥30 min before STD; defect-to-report time ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: FliteDeck EFB walk-around checklists are not connected to AMOS defect recording — items found during walk-around must be re-entered manually in the aircraft tech log, creating duplication and potential omission

l4_steps.name: Confirm final weight & balance load sheet
l4_steps.input: Final passenger count, cargo weights, fuel load, trim settings
l4_steps.output: Signed load sheet; CG within envelope confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Load sheet issued ≤15 min before STD; CG deviation from plan <0.5% MAC
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute passenger no-shows or late cargo add-ons require load sheet recalculation in Altéa — under the 10-min gate departure pressure window, rushed W&B recalculations increase the risk of CG errors

l4_steps.name: Obtain ATC clearance and departure slot
l4_steps.input: Filed flight plan, ATIS, ATFM slot allocation
l4_steps.output: ATC route clearance; CTOT confirmed or delay calculated
l4_steps.kpi: Clearance received ≥5 min before pushback; ATFM slot adherence ≥94%
l4_steps.pain_point: ATFM slot allocations from EUROCONTROL NMOC (or FAA EDCT in North America) are issued dynamically and can shift within the last 10 min — ACARS delivery to cockpit adds latency vs. VHF voice clearance, risking slot miss
